correctness.rationale: For every n>=4 and arbitrary scan, cyclic rotation and label symmetry reduce the deleted edge to positions 1 and k+1. Exact polynomial row equations and unimodular elimination yield H_{k,m}; its determinant and entry gcd yield d1=gcd(x^k+1,(x^n+1)/(x+1)) and d2=(x^k+1)(x^m+1)/d1. A full two-adic exponent check gives the asserted fixed-space dimensions, minimal-polynomial order and primitive orbit census. Directly counted gap placements give n(n-2)! scans per gap. Boundary k=1 is handled separately, and the finite matrix, polynomial, orbit and scan enumerations in verify.py reproduced the exact predictions (5,910 independently checked scans in each of two graph families, 695,472 scan–states in each family; 15,438 paired matrix/polynomial checks). These finite checks do not substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: The statement is an explicit invariant-factor and all-scan orbit classification for K_n minus exactly one edge, including a uniform scan-gap law and a cross-graph comparison to C_n. The known C_n census is credited and used, but it does not imply its extension to the dense deleted-edge graph. Inspected primary sources treat fixed-graph scan equivalence (Macauley–Mortveit), general sequential linear system methods (Chen–Reidys), and cycle graphs (Defant). No examined text states the deleted-edge clique result. Published semantic queries for deleted-edge clique, Coxeter synonyms, cycle equivalence, scan frequencies and exact fixed counts returned no covering statement. Historical equivalent formulations remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: A historical Coxeter-transformation theorem for near-complete graphs might imply the invariant factors in different notation; no definitive universal literature exclusion is possible.
A directly inaccessible or unindexed document could contain a stronger equivalent statement.
Conjugacy is set-theoretic from cycle populations, not a constructive linear conjugacy.

value.rationale: The problem compares naturally extremal graph topologies in a finite invertible dynamical system: a one-edge-deleted complete graph and an ordinary cycle. The exact correspondence of cycle populations despite divergent scan statistics is a motivated structural invariant; uniform counts versus Eulerian counts expose a quantifiable scheduling sensitivity. The new dense-graph Smith-factor derivation and closed all-period orbit census solve a natural infinite-family problem, not a routine reparametrization or arbitrary finite lookup.
